title: Fourier Series: Drawing With Rotating Circles
production_path_basis: The showcase library is explicitly mute for this production cycle.
audience: Curious general learners with graph and basic trigonometry familiarity
central_message: A periodic signal can be reconstructed by adding simple rotating components whose frequency, amplitude, and phase have distinct roles.
takeaway: The spectrum is a recipe, and each harmonic has the same identity across geometry, formula, and plotted signal.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
mathematical_depth: conceptual introduction with one canonical square-wave series
visual_direction: dark editorial canvas, luminous harmonic palette, persistent cross-view color identity
pacing: purposeful visual beats with short readable statements and repeated state changes
constraints: no claim of uniform convergence at a discontinuity
no decorative representation without explanatory purpose
success_criteria: stable harmonic colors span all representations
at least three partial sums are compared
Gibbs behavior is accurately distinguished from simple disappearance
preview render is visually inspected at representative timestamps
